response.sql:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT p.ID, p.SEX,
           AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
           AVG(l.APTT - l.PT) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
), sex_averages AS (
    SELECT SEX,
           AVG(avg_alb_minus_tp) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
           AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM patient_averages
    GROUP BY SEX
), sex_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS mean_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM sex_averages
)
SELECT AVG(s.avg_alb_minus_tp) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
       AVG(s.avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt,
       AVG(s.avg_aptt_minus_pt - m.mean_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_excess_over_mean
FROM sex_averages AS s
CROSS JOIN sex_mean AS m
WHERE s.avg_aptt_minus_pt > m.mean_aptt_minus_pt;

assumptions.assumption: Each requested patient average uses the lab rows where both values in the difference are non-NULL; SQL arithmetic and AVG ignore NULL differences. Sex-level and final averages likewise ignore NULL averages, while NULL and blank SEX values form their own groups.
